A1_rft_orthogonal.verdict: TRUE (orthogonal); but it is the classical real/trigonometric DFT (rescaled numpy.fft.rfft), so 'first construction' is not supported.

A2_theorem1.claim: (1) any n columns of Phi_1 independent; (2) C_1 strictly equiangular, S_1 orthogonal
A2_theorem1.verdict: Holds in exact arithmetic for every tested m (C_1 equiangular, S_1 orthogonal), BUT the smallest singular value over n-column subsets collapses roughly 10x per +2 in m (see min_singular_value), so 'maximal robustness' gives no numerical robustness to noise for realistic m.

A4_orthogonal_system_theorem.claim: x* = C^+ d when the curtailed equations have zero constant terms
A4_orthogonal_system_theorem.verdict: TRUE but elementary: with orthogonal rows, A^-1 b = sum_i a_i b_i/|a_i|^2, so dropping rows with b_i = 0 changes nothing. Exactness needs the UNKNOWN coefficients to be zero, i.e. the signal must be exactly band/sparsity-limited.

A5_hadamard_example.claim: x* recovered from 7 of 8 Hadamard equations by TV-minimising LP
A5_hadamard_example.verdict: NOT RECOVERED: the curtailed row is the constant (DC) row and TV is blind to constants, so x*+c is TV-minimal for every c; the LP returned x*+1 (same TV). The example is ill-posed.

A7_maximum_accuracy_theorem.claim: MAC attains the maximum accuracy that the samples can provide
A7_maximum_accuracy_theorem.verdict: FALSE as an optimality statement: the proof only restates Parseval (||x-x'|| = ||A x - A x'|| for ANY estimate x'); no minimisation over estimators is performed. Plain linear interpolation from the SAME samples is more accurate on this piecewise-smooth signal.

A8_gibbs.claim: transform expression never fails, even for discontinuous f
A8_gibbs.verdict: FALSE pointwise: MAC rings at every jump (14-18% of the jump height here, above the 8.95% Gibbs limit of Fourier partial sums because of aliasing) and the overshoot does not vanish as the sampling rate changes.

A9_40x_claim.verdict: Arithmetic correct for Lena only (40.18x); the other images give 17.5x and 12.1x. The CNN numbers (ReconNet, CVPR'16) come from random Gaussian block projections, a different measurement model, so the comparison is not like-for-like.

A10_lsb_point_samples.claim: LSB x*=C^+d applied to the partial system obtained by keeping time samples
A10_lsb_point_samples.verdict: Literal LSB on time-sample curtailment returns the ZERO-FILLED signal (min-norm coefficients <=> min-norm signal for orthogonal A). The working MAC must therefore be spectral zero-padding (trigonometric interpolation).
